paper.title: FT-WBC: Learning Fault-Tolerant Whole-Body Control for Legged Loco-Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct fault-tolerant legged loco-manipulation study with simulation and physical failure injection.

sections_read.purpose: Identify actuator-fault risk during whole-body manipulation.
Inspect fault estimation and posture adaptation.

research_question: Can fault awareness preserve both survival and useful arm workspace during legged loco-manipulation?
contributions: Fault estimator and posture adaptation modules integrated with whole-body control.

method.summary: PPO learns a whole-body policy with simulated actuator weakening; an estimator localizes the failed joint and a posture module reduces loading toward the faulty support.
assumptions: A single dominant actuator fault occurs.
Faults resemble torque weakening or locked joints.

datasets: Simulated partial and complete weakening curricula
embodiments: Unitree Go2 with Airbot Play arm
study_context.sample_or_scale: 1,000 randomized simulation trials; 20 physical trials per height and fault condition.

evaluation.design: Compares Robo-Duet, no-estimator, no-posture-adaptation and full policies under 12 joint faults; tests unseen locked faults physically.

findings.finding: The controller trades workspace/aggressive completion for survival as faults become severe, including unseen locked faults.
findings.scope: Single-joint faults on one quadruped-arm system.

author_stated.limitation: The method addresses only single-actuator failures and real tests are stationary-base or sequential move-then-manipulate tasks.

reader_inferred.boundary: Fault tolerance does not yet cover simultaneous faults or manipulation during continuous walking.
reader_inferred.basis: These exclusions are stated explicitly in the limitations section.

transfer_boundary: Applies to isolated lower-limb actuator degradation; multi-fault and continuously dynamic manipulation remain unvalidated.

design_strengths: Tests unmodeled locked faults after training only on weakening.
design_risks: Safety claims are based on one hardware platform.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Ablations share training and task setup; the primary baseline lacks fault awareness by design.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Separate survival and completion metrics expose the safety-performance tradeoff.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Fault curriculum and trial counts are described; exact hardware fault injection details are critical for replication.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Limited to single-joint lower-limb faults and sequential tasks.

evidence_cards.claim: Under an unseen locked-joint fault at the most demanding placement height, FT-WBC retained 70% survival but only 45% task success, reflecting an explicit survival-first posture policy.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports fault-aware deployment while exposing the safety-versus-completion tradeoff.
evidence_cards.summary: The real-world analysis directly attributes reduced completion to conservative posture limits that preserve the degraded support polygon.
evidence_cards.source_context: At the extreme height, our framework still guarantees a 70% survival rate even under severe locked conditions, demonstrating strong adaptation to out-of-distribution actuator failures. While the task success rate drops to 45%, this occurs because the PAM conservatively restricts the extreme upward pitch to prevent the CoM from escaping the degraded support polygon.

quantitative.comparator: unseen locked fault at extreme height

verification.rationale: The cited passage reports both percentages and the conservative posture mechanism; the claim is limited to the extreme-height locked-fault condition.
